intent: The intent of this schedule is to permit 4-storey apartments to provide a transition in residential neighbourhoods between higher building forms and ground-oriented building forms. The emphasis is on creating of a variety of dwelling unit sizes, including those appropriate for families with children. Townhouses are only permitted in combination with an apartment building and on exceptionally deep sites. [...] Without limitation, applicable Council policies and guidelines for consideration include the RM-9, RM-9A and RM-9B Guidelines.

clauses.text: The intent of this schedule is to permit 4-storey apartments to provide a transition in residential neighbourhoods between higher building forms and ground-oriented building forms. The emphasis is on creating of a variety of dwelling unit sizes, including those appropriate for families with children. Townhouses are only permitted in combination with an apartment building and on exceptionally deep sites. [...] Without limitation, applicable Council policies and guidelines for consideration include the RM-9, RM-9A and RM-9B Guidelines.

The table below provides an overview of the outright and conditional approval uses in the RM-9A district, categorized by the minimum site area required, where applicable. Applicable density, form and placement regulations in section 3 of this schedule are cross-referenced in the third column.

All outright and conditional approval uses are subject to all other provisions of this by-law, including Section 2, Section 10 and Section 11, and compliance with the regulations of this schedule including section 2.2. [...] The uses identified in the table below as outright approval uses are permitted in these districts and will be issued a permit. [...] The uses identified in the table below as conditional approval uses may be approved in these districts by the Director of Planning, with or without conditions, if the Director of Planning considers: [...] Uses are listed under their general land use category. Applicable use-specific regulations in section 2.2 of this schedule are cross-referenced in the third column. Cross-references to applicable use-specific regulations are provided for information purposes only and do not form part of this by-law.
the intent of this schedule and all applicable Council policies and guidelines; and
the submission of any advisory group, property owner or tenant.
The Director of Planning may permit more than 1 apartment building on a site if the Director of Planning considers the intent of this schedule and all applicable Council policies and guidelines.

Apartment in combination with townhouse may be permitted on sites with a depth of 45.7 m or more, if the townhouse is located at the rear of the site and if the Director of Planning considers the intent of this schedule and all applicable Council policies and guidelines.
Duplex with secondary suite, in combination with another principal building, must have no more than 1 secondary suite for each dwelling unit.

Laneway house is subject to the R1-1 District Schedule and must be in combination with a single detached house, a single detached house with secondary suite, or a child day care facility, which is the only principal building on the site.
The only non-dwelling use permitted in a mixed-use residential building is neighbourhood grocery store.
Multiple conversion dwelling containing 2 dwelling units is permitted as an outright approval use if:
there are no additions to the building;
no housekeeping or sleeping units are created;
the development complies with sections 3.6.2.6, 3.6.2.7 and 4.3 of this schedule; and
no development permit is issued until the requisite permits required by other by-laws that relate to design, construction and safety of buildings are issuable.

Multiple conversion dwelling that is not permitted as an outright approval use, resulting from the conversion of a building existing as of May 27, 2014, may be permitted as a conditional approval use if:

the Director of Planning considers the quality and liveability of the resulting units, the suitability of the building for conversion in terms of age and size, and the impact of the conversion on adjacent properties;
there are no additions to buildings constructed on or after January 1, 1940, except additions up to 5 m² used as exits;
no housekeeping or sleeping units are created; and
there are no more than 3 dwelling units.

Principal dwelling unit with lock-off unit may be permitted only in a multiple dwelling and there may be no more than 1 lock-off unit for every 3 principal dwelling units, except that the Director of Planning may permit a higher ratio after considering the intent of this schedule and all applicable Council policies and guidelines.
Where a single detached house or single detached house with secondary suite is the only principal building on the site:
it must comply with the R1-1 District Schedule; and
the lot must have been on record in the Land Title Office prior to January 16, 2018.
Single detached house with secondary suite, in combination with another principal building, must have no more than 1 secondary suite for each dwelling unit.
Community care or assisted living facility - class A must comply with the regulations that apply to this use in the R1-1 district.

Farmers’ market may be permitted if the Director of Planning considers the appropriateness of the use with respect to compatibility with nearby sites, parking, traffic, noise, hours of operation, size of facility and pedestrian amenity.
Accessory buildings customarily ancillary to any use listed in section 2.1 of this schedule, other than those ancillary to multiple dwelling, are permitted as an outright approval use if:
no accessory building exceeds 3.7 m in height, measured to: [...] provided that no portion of an accessory building exceeds 4.6 m in building height;
the highest point of a flat roof,
the deck line of a mansard roof, or
the mean height between the eaves and the ridge of a gable, hip or gambrel roof,
all accessory buildings are located:
within 7.9 m of the ultimate rear property line,
at least 3.6 m from the ultimate centre line of any rear or flanking lane, and
at least 1.5 m from a flanking street;
the total floor area of all accessory buildings, measured to the extreme outer limits of the building, does not exceed 48 m2;
the combined width for all accessory buildings does not exceed 80% of the width of the site at the rear property line;
the separation from any residential building is at least 3.7 m; and
roof decks and decks are not located on an accessory building.
Accessory buildings customarily ancillary to multiple dwelling may be permitted as a conditional approval use if:
no accessory building exceeds 3.7 m in height, measured to: [...] except that no portion of an accessory building exceeds 4.6 m in building height;
the highest point of a flat roof,
the deck line of a mansard roof, or
the mean height between the eaves and the ridge of a gable, hip or gambrel roof,
all accessory buildings are located:
within 7.9 m of the ultimate rear property line,
at least 3.6 m from the ultimate centre line of any rear or flanking lane, and
at least 1.5 m from a flanking street;

the total floor area of all accessory buildings, measured to the extreme outer limits of the building, does not exceed 48 m2, except that the Director of Planning may increase the total floor area of all accessory buildings to a maximum of 24 m2 for each dwelling unit, not including lock-off units, if the Director of Planning considers the intent of this schedule and all applicable Council policies and guidelines;

the building width for all accessory buildings does not exceed 30% of the width of the site at the rear property line, except that the Director of Planning may increase the maximum building width up to 80%, if the Director of Planning considers the intent of this schedule and all applicable Council policies and guidelines;
the separation from any residential building is at least 3.7 m; and
roof decks and decks are not located on an accessory building.
Accessory parking spaces customarily ancillary to any outright approval use listed in section 2.1 above must comply with the provisions of section 2.2.13(b) above.

Child day care facility conversion dwelling is subject to the regulations, variations and relaxations that apply to: [...] This section contains density, form and placement regulations organized by use.
single detached house, when the child day care facility conversion dwelling was converted from a single detached house; and
single detached house with secondary suite, when the child day care facility conversion dwelling was converted from a single detached house with secondary suite.
